secondary.$description: Secondary foreground color. Light darkened neutral.600 -> neutral.700 (FIX-CONTRAST-DEBT-01): neutral.600 measured 4.38:1 on background.secondary (neutral.100), under AA 4.5:1.

hover.$description: Hover foreground color. Dark brightened neutral.300 -> neutral.200 (FIX-CONTRAST-DEBT-01): neutral.300 measured 3.60:1 on background.hover dark (neutral.700), under AA 4.5:1. Mirrors the light direction — hover strengthens the text.

onColor.$description: Foreground color for text on saturated colored/accent fills. Fixed white in both themes (not theme-primary text) so it clears WCAG AA on accent/strong backgrounds (4.68:1 on red.500). Mirrors foreground.on.brand.

plain.$description: Plain text in syntax highlighting Theme-aware for WCAG AA against background.secondary (neutral.100 light / neutral.800 dark) per FIX-CONTRAST-PALETTE-REPAIR-01: ramp step >=700 in light, <=300 in dark.

disabled.$description: Disabled foreground color. Bumped from neutral.300/500 to neutral.500/400 to meet 3:1 against background.disabled (neutral.200/700). WCAG SC 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls from contrast minimums, but unreadable disabled labels are usability debt — this satisfies AA_LARGE (3:1) so disabled state stays visibly de-emphasized without becoming invisible.

inverse.$description: Inverse foreground color — the label color used INSIDE colored action surfaces (primary/danger buttons). The colored surface keeps its hue across light and dark themes, so the inverse label stays light in both. NOT the inverse of foreground.primary — use foreground.on-inverse for a surface painted background.inverse.

on-inverse.$description: Label color for a surface painted background.inverse (tooltips, inverted callouts). background.inverse flips per theme — mode.dark in light, mode.light in dark — so this flips the OPPOSITE way to stay readable. Pair the two together. Do NOT use foreground.inverse here: it is light in both themes, which renders light-on-light in dark mode.
